subject: Tarik Skubal
title: Tarik Skubal Mets contract: How big is it? 9 years, $450 million
answer: Two-time American League Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal has agreed to a nine-year, $450 million contract with the New York Mets, according to reports from ESPN and MLB.com on Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. The deal averages $50 million a season, the most ever for a pitcher, and is pending a physical.
in_the_news: It is the richest contract ever given to a pitcher, beating Yoshinobu Yamamoto's $325 million, and it lands days before baseball's labor agreement expires on Dec. 1, when owners are expected to lock players out and free agency could freeze.
body:
Skubal, who turned 30 on Nov. 20, chose the Mets over the Toronto Blue Jays, San Diego Padres and Los Angeles Dodgers after meeting with teams in California the week before, ESPN reported. MLB.com reported that the contract has no opt-outs and includes no-trade protection. The Mets had not confirmed the agreement because it was still pending a physical.

The money puts Skubal in rare company. Only Juan Soto, who signed with the Mets for 15 years and $765 million in December 2024, Shohei Ohtani and Vladimir Guerrero Jr. have bigger total deals, and only Ohtani, Kyle Tucker and Soto earn more per season, according to MLB.com. The previous record average salary for a pitcher was Max Scherzer's $43.3 million, also with the Mets, in 2021.

How a ninth-round pick got here: 2018 — Detroit drafts Skubal in the ninth round out of Seattle University, a year after Tommy John surgery. 2024 — he wins the pitching Triple Crown (18 wins, 2.39 ERA, 228 strikeouts) and a unanimous AL Cy Young. 2025 — a second straight Cy Young after leading the league with a 2.21 ERA. February 2026 — an arbitrator awards him $32 million for the season instead of the Tigers' $19 million offer. May 2026 — a minor elbow procedure to remove loose bodies; he is back on the mound by mid-June. Early August 2026 — the struggling Tigers trade him to the Dodgers for three prospects. Nov. 22, 2026 — the Mets deal.

For New York, the signing fills the biggest hole on a club that missed the playoffs two seasons in a row and entered the winter with a thin rotation. President of baseball operations David Stearns has said the team is still looking for help at first base and in the bullpen. Skubal finished 2026 at 12-7 with a 2.72 ERA across Detroit and Los Angeles.

What comes next: once the physical is done, the Mets are expected to announce the deal formally. Any other moves the team wants to make quickly will have to come before the collective bargaining agreement expires on Dec. 1; a lockout would halt transactions involving major league players until a new deal is reached.

faq.a: Not yet. ESPN and MLB.com reported the agreement through sources on Nov. 22, 2026; the Mets were waiting on a physical before announcing it.

faq.q: Is Skubal's contract the biggest ever for a pitcher?
faq.a: Yes. At $450 million it tops Yoshinobu Yamamoto's 12-year, $325 million deal with the Dodgers from December 2023, and its $50 million average is the highest for a pitcher.

faq.q: Does Skubal's contract have an opt-out?
faq.a: According to MLB.com, no. The deal runs nine years without opt-outs and includes no-trade protection.

faq.q: Why did Skubal leave the Dodgers?
faq.a: He was only with Los Angeles for the final two months of 2026 after a trade and became a free agent after the season. ESPN reported the Dodgers did not make him an offer before the expected lockout.
